title: Canary release scratchpad - Leah Chen
body:
Context:
- Target: rolling out serving-runtime v2.3.1 (inference kernel + kv-cache fixes) to hosted-api fleet and dedicated pools. This is mostly a stability/latency improvement but we need to watch for regressions in long-context chat workloads.
- Motivation: several customer reports of increased token latency on >8k context. v2.3.1 includes a kernel fallback for certain attention patterns plus safer KV eviction that should reduce tail latency.

High-level plan (personal scratchpad):
1) Prep (today - infra/QA)
   - bake image: serving-runtime:v2.3.1-canary (tagged) -> done (build#482)
   - smoke tests: basic text-gen, chat, embeddings parity -> PASS locally
   - perf tests: synthetic 4k/16k sequences (0.5k samples) -> 4k median improved, 16k tail slightly worse on one hw pool (need investigate)
   - QA checklist: run regression evals on core prompt set (eval-suite v2026-02-20) -> pending full run

2) Canary rollout (this doc)
   - Phase A: internal traffic only (engineer & automated tests) -> 1% of internal production token volume routed to v2.3.1-canary via routing-policy canary-internal
   - Phase B: 0.1% external customer traffic (non-critical customers) for 24h
   - Phase C: ramp to 1% customer traffic over 48h if stable
   - Phase D: optional burst to 5% for 2h to validate autoscale and heat up caches
   - Phase E: evaluate, decide to promote to stable tag and start rollout or rollback

Runbook / checklist (quick):
- Before Phase A:
  - Update rollout config in Console: route_table=canary-internal, pin_model_flag=false, max_inflight=1000
  - Create trace sampling rule: sample_rate=1% for canary-internal
  - Add temporary dashboard: dashboard://canary-v2-3-1 (copy of serving-runtime/main)
  - Notify on-call (SRE) & PM slack (#releases)
- During Phase A:
  - Watch error rate (5xx) and latency p50/p95/p99 for tokens and requests (Datadog monitors): if error_rate > baseline + 0.5% OR p99 > baseline + 30% => pause rollout
  - Check KV cache hit rate, memory pressure (gpu mem spare < 1GB) -> alert
  - Monitor model outputs for hallucination/regression via eval hooks (sample 100 chat threads/day)
- Phase B/C ramp:
  - Increase only if Phase A stable for 4h and no critical alerts
  - Use progressive pinning: pin small subset of routes first (chat-long-context, codegen)
  - Confirm autoscaling behavior in Dedicated pools (scale-out latencies under 15s)

Rollback criteria (hard):
- sustained 5xx increase > baseline + 1% for 30m
- p99 token latency increase > baseline + 50% for 30m
- memory OOMs or repeated KV eviction thrash causing degraded throughput
- customer-reported high-severity incidents (pager)

Rollback steps:
1) Flip routing policy to previous stable tag (serving-runtime:v2.3.0-stable) using quick-fallback policy
2) Abort scale-up jobs related to canary nodes
3) Create incident oncall doc + assign owner (usually release lead)
4) Collect traces, core dumps, perf profiles, and link to PR & jira (JIRA-3487)

Version pinning notes:
- We will pin only on a per-route basis initially. Do NOT pin entire fleet unless promoting to GA.
- Pin flag name: runtime.pin_version -> set to v2.3.1 on subset routes via Console API. Example curl:
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/admin/pin -d '{"route":"chat-long","version":"v2.3.1"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
- Keep pin TTL=24h during canary; make permanent only after full verification and release notes published.

Telemetry queries to run (notes):
- Datadog: query p99_latency{env:prod,route:chat-long,version:v2.3.1-canary} and compare to baseline v2.3.0-stable
- BigQuery: sample request logs for generation length >4096 tokens and examine time-to-first-byte and total-token-latency
- Eval harness: run eval-suite/long-context/regression against golden set -> record BLEU/ROUGE style metrics + safety checks

Open questions / unknowns (needs answers):
- Why did perf test show slightly worse 16k tail on pool-b? Hypothesis: kernel selection fallback triggering fallback path slower on A100-40GB. Action: Samir to re-run micro-bench on A100-40Gb with detailed perf counters (PR #1123 mentions this).
- Are there any customers pinned to v2.3.0 that will be affected by traffic routing rules? Need to cross-check customer pinning table (product-ops)
- Confirm whether dedicated customers have their own pin override (tenant-level override) before we flip routing policy.

Notes to self / TODOs: 
- Run full eval-suite overnight and attach results to JIRA-3487 (leah)
- Draft short release note (1 paragraph) for #releases with expected risk & rollback plan (Maya to review)
- Add canary alert runbook to Confluence (link above) -> include run commands and example queries
- If stable, coordinate with infra to tag docker image as v2.3.1-stable and kick GA rollout next Tues

Quick log of last runs:
- 2026-02-25 09:10 - build produced, smoke tests PASS (leah)
- 2026-02-25 12:45 - perf run: 4k median -12%, 16k p99 +8% on pool-b (Samir investigating)
- 2026-02-26 03:20 - manual edge-case chat test found minor tokenization diff in codegen prompts (filed as JIRA-3492)

Slack threads / refs: #releases (pin pinned), #sre-oncall, /cc @samir @noah

Quick contact list:
- Release lead: Leah Chen (me)
- SRE oncall: Noah Kim
- Perf lead: Samir Patel
- QA: Maya Singh

End of scratchpad. Keep this doc informal; will tidy into canary-runbook v2 if we promote.
